newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended softer on Wednesday continuing the weakness begun before the close on Tuesday when shares slid on a lower Wall Street opening.
Gold shares were softer, depressed by a dull bullion price which had slipped some $3 since Monday to trade around the $340 an ounce level.
Dealers said the market's performance on Wednesday had been disappointing given that Wall Street ended at a new high on Tuesday night, albeit on a slim 10 point rise, and the London bourse was firm.

But local factors, in particular ponr results from two of South Africa's biggest retail and construction firms -- sectors which dealers said were good indicators of the country's level of economic activity -- weighed down stocks.
Retail share Edgars on Tuesday posted its first drop in full-year earnings in 10 years, dealers said.
Building and construction firm PPC also posted lower earnings saying it had been hurt by weak cement demand and forecast lower growth for the second half of the year.
"Edgars was down nearly seven percent on bad results. This reflects badly on the stores sector and consumer demand particularly. We had negative growth from PPC as well.
"Here you have two of the big companies in their sectors coming out and saying things are not all that good out there," said Johan Marais," a director at Societe General Frankel Pollak.
Edgars shares on Wednesday lost 800 cents to 102 rand after touching five-month lows of 98 rand during the day. PPC ended steady at 69.50 rand.
First National Bank on Wednesday reported results slightly below analysts' expectations. Shares ended down 30 cents at 31.60 rand.
The 100 percent industrial index lost 65.1 points to 8,503.6 points, depressing the all-share index 51.2 points to 7,160.7.
Gold shares were largely ignored on the lacklustre bullion price leaving the all gold index 23.0 points lower at 1,189.3.
Dealers said volumes traded were below average excluding a large bookover in Gensec shares worth nearly 230 million rand.
However, over the week volumes had been large boosted by asset swaps, large foreign deals and some futures activity.
They said the direction the market would take on Thursday was difficult to call as it had largely diverged from Wall Street's lead in recent days.
"It is difficult to say what the market will look like tomorrow (Thursday). It dropped sharply today and we have probably seen the worst," one said.
Near-term gold share futures also were weak in late trade on a softer bullion price. Industrial futures also joined the gloom in the cash market.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,645/60 from 6,708, the industrial contract was at 8,356/65 from 8,425 and the gold contract was at 845/51 from 860.
